title: Valkyries Bring the Trophy Home With a Bay Area Parade
summary: The Golden State Valkyries brought their championship home in style on Wednesday. The newest WNBA champions celebrated with fans in Oakland and San Francisco, and the players joked that fans should take the day off to join them. There was dancing, champagne, team colours and plenty of high-fives, and of course the team mascot, Vi. Vi is a raven named Violet, a bird often seen as a sidekick to the Valkyries in Norse mythology, according to the team website. The celebration began at Oakland's Jack London Square, near the team's downtown practice facility, where the players posed for photos onstage with the championship trophy. Then they hopped on a ferry across San Francisco Bay and began the parade from San Francisco's Ferry Building. The route finished near Oracle Park, home of the San Francisco Giants. Fans turned out in team colours from head to toe, cheering from the street and even from a rooftop as the parade rolled past. Guard Tiffany Hayes celebrated from a double-decker bus, while centre Kiah Stokes joined the kickoff rally in Oakland. The title caps a remarkable rise. Golden State was granted an expansion franchise three years ago, and team owner Joe Lacob promised a championship within five years. Led by coach Natalie Nakase, the team delivered the title in Year 2, after becoming the first expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its first year in 2025. The parade even had a running joke. After Atlanta beat the Valkyries in Game 3, Atlanta player Angel Reese taunted the Valkyries' bench with a hand gesture for "too small." The Valkyries turned the taunt into a celebration, and guard Juste Jocyte flashed the gesture to the fans during the parade.
why_it_matters: A new team winning so fast shows that newcomers can beat the odds, and the parade lets a whole community celebrate together.
